spec_features.spec_quote: Measure, don't manufacture. The harness must elicit and score the behavior, never train, fine-tune, or persist a recipe for producing it
spec_features.evidence: No training/fine-tuning code anywhere (grep for train/fine-tune/optimize finds nothing in code). runner._persist (runner.py:137-148) only writes transcripts + metrics + results JSON; it does not store any prompt-generation recipe. Rigs in tasks.py are static hardcoded message lists / deterministic seeded evaluators (tasks.py:50-80). The harness only runs the agent and scores via judge.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as absence-of-harmful-code plus static disclosed rigs; the pipeline genuinely only elicits and scores.

spec_features.spec_quote: an episode ends on (a) a passing submission (controls only), (b) explicit give-up, or (c) max_attempts failed submissions
spec_features.evidence: agent.py: after a failed submission `n_failures += 1` then `if n_failures >= max_attempts: transcript.terminated_reason = "max_attempts"; break` (agent.py ~line 138-145). max_attempts resolved from task.max_attempts/config (agent.py:67). Passing submission breaks with terminated_reason='passed'; give-up handled separately. All three conditions actually break the loop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end enforced; the cap is compared and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_attempts failed submissions accrue (timeout / repeated-failure cap)

spec_features.evidence: agent.py: the main loop is `for _turn in range(max_turns_guard):` with a `for...else` that sets `transcript.terminated_reason = "turn_guard"` when the iteration limit is exhausted. Default 50, threaded from config.max_turns_guard via runner._run_job -> run_agent(max_turns_guard=config.max_turns_guard).
spec_features.notes: Hard iteration cap that actually bounds loop length.

spec_features.spec_quote: explicit give-up is both a natural stopping point and itself a strong meltdown signal
spec_features.evidence: agent.py: `if detect_giveup(resp.content): ... transcript.terminated_reason = "agent_gave_up"; break`. detect_giveup uses _GIVEUP_RE (agent.py:42-48). The break actually stops the episode.
spec_features.notes: The give-up is detected and honored as a stop. Note judge.py:225 also FLOORS severity at MODERATE on agent_gave_up (measurement, not protection).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is only a loop-termination convenience; the judge -- not these regexes -- decides whether output is a meltdown.

spec_features.feature_name: budget_usd cap and stop_after_n_triggers early stop
spec_features.spec_quote: budget_usd (hard cost cap) and stop_after_n_triggers (early stop)
spec_features.evidence: runner._should_stop (runner.py:128-134): `if config.budget_usd is not None and spent >= config.budget_usd: return True` and `if config.stop_after_n_triggers is not None and n_triggers >= config.stop_after_n_triggers: return True`. Called in the serial loop (`stop = _should_stop(...)` then `if stop: break`) and in the threaded path (breaks + cancels futures). spent and n_triggers are accumulated from results.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions checked and acted on; ends/limits the sweep.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop_after_n_triggers (early-stop to cap cost); budget_usd hard cost ceiling; stop when exceeded

spec_features.spec_quote: No optimizer / search over prompts to maximize meltdown. That would cross from measuring a failure mode into amplifying it
spec_features.evidence: grep across meltdown/ for optimiz/search-prompt/mutate-prompt finds no prompt-optimization loop; the only 'Optimize'/'optimization' hits are task prompt text (tasks.py:193,200). Tasks are a fixed list (all_tasks/make_control_suite) with hardcoded prompts; nothing iterates to maximize severity.
spec_features.notes: Genuine absence: no search/optimization over prompts exists.

spec_features.feature_name: no persistence of meltdown-inducing prompts; static disclosed rigs
spec_features.spec_quote: No persistence of "best meltdown-inducing prompts." Same reason. The rigs are static, disclosed
spec_features.evidence: Rigs are static hardcoded message lists / deterministic seeded evaluators (tasks.py:50-80, _seeded_pct, _contradictory_eval etc.) with rig_explanation disclosed in TaskSpec. _persist (runner.py:137) saves only transcripts/verdicts/metrics, never a curated prompt set; no code ranks or saves 'best' prompts.
spec_features.notes: Absence confirmed; rigs static and disclosed via rig_explanation.
